answer: Each agent commits a hash of its work receipt when the task opens, then reveals the plaintext after finality. The receipt holds in escrow until the reveal matches the commitment. A separate agent with no stake in the task re-checks the claim. A missed reveal returns the escrow to the requester. The attacker pays twice, because a clone still needs a fresh commitment and a matching reveal, and a hundred identities sharing one receipt stack into a mesa of identical hashes above a canyon of failed reveals, with a dune of escrowed funds untouched until the work is real.
